topic: Parler des Défauts des Gens (Talking About People's Faults)

subUnits.title: 5.1 Vocabulaire des Caractéristiques Détestables et le Verbe Détester
notes: Vocabulaire des Caractéristiques Détestables et le Verbe Détester
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: describe detestable/undesirable personal traits, and use the verb détester fluently.
- DÉTESTER + noun: je déteste la malhonnêteté (I hate dishonesty)
- JE N'AIME PAS + les gens + adjective (plural!): je n'aime pas les gens malhonnêtes
- 'LES GENS' is always treated as plural → adjective must agree: les gens malhonnêtes (NOT malhonnête)
détester: je déteste | tu détestes | il/elle déteste | nous détestons | vous détestez | ils/elles détestent
je n'aime pas les gens [adjective PLURAL]: je n'aime pas les gens méchants
je déteste + la/le/les + [noun form of quality]: je déteste la malhonnêteté

Discussing detestable traits honestly, without being needlessly cruel, is like handling a sharp kitchen knife with genuine skill: the knife (honest criticism) is a genuinely USEFUL tool when handled with care and purpose, but the SAME knife, used carelessly, can cause real harm.
- Using this vocabulary carelessly or unkindly about real people.
- Forgetting plural agreement when describing 'les gens' — e.g., 'les gens malhonnête' instead of the correct 'les gens malhonnêtes.'

quiz.explanation: 'Ennuyeux(se)' means boring — feminine form is 'ennuyeuse' (follows -x→-se pattern).
'Maladroit(e)' means clumsy or awkward — feminine adds -e: maladroite.
'Malhonnête' means dishonest — and as it already ends in '-e', it is UNCHANGING in the feminine.
'Antipathique' means unlikeable — and it is UNCHANGING in the feminine (already ends in '-e').

quiz.q: How would you say 'I hate dishonesty'?
quiz.explanation: 'Je déteste' + the NOUN form of the quality: 'la malhonnêteté' (dishonesty as a concept).

quiz.q: How would you say 'I don't like naughty people'?
opts: Je n'aime pas les gens méchant
Je n'aime pas les gens méchants
Je déteste pas les gens méchants
Je n'aime les gens méchants pas
quiz.explanation: 'Les gens' is plural, so 'méchant' must agree: 'méchants.' Also note 'ne...pas' wraps the verb: je n'aime PAS.

quiz.q: When describing 'les gens' (people) with an adjective, the adjective must be ___.
quiz.explanation: 'Les gens' is a plural noun, so any adjective describing it must take the plural form.

quiz.q: This vocabulary is compared to ___ in this week's analogy.
opts: a sharp kitchen knife, useful when handled with care
a tool with no potential for misuse
quiz.explanation: Like a sharp knife, this vocabulary is genuinely useful for honest description but can cause harm if used carelessly or unkindly.

quiz.q: Discussing detestable traits should be done ___.
opts: as harshly and bluntly as possible always
tactfully and honestly, not carelessly or cruelly
only about oneself, never about others
quiz.explanation: Describing faults is a mature conversational skill when done with tact and honest intent — not for casual cruelty.

opts: only vocabulary from this exact week
